## Goal
- Establish Ivan Perez as end-to-end IVX owner while Rork remains an authorized developer/deployer with 0% ownership or control over code, credentials, infrastructure, and business accounts.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Never delete, overwrite, or alter IVX code, GitHub history, production data, database, AWS resources, or deployments while resolving ownership controls.
- Rork may develop, create code, and deploy only at the owner’s request; owner retains all credentials, billing, source, recovery, and final approval.
- Do not request or receive AWS/root login, password, MFA codes, recovery codes, access keys, tokens, or secrets.
- Do not overstate certification results or lower the score by source-only edits without evidence.
- User is upset by repeated proof requests; accept already provided Render and AWS-root evidence and avoid asking for further evidence unless technically indispensable.

## Progress
### Done
- Verified GitHub repository control:
  ```text
  repository: ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform
  branch: main
  owner: ibb142
  permissions: admin=true, maintain=true, push=true, triage=true, pull=true
  default_branch: main
  visibility: private
  ```
- Verified Render production source configuration:
  ```text
  service: srv-d7t9ivreo5us73ftose0
  name: ivx-holdings-platform
  repo: https://github.com/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform
  branch: main
  environment: docker
  url: https://ivx-holdings-platform.onrender.com
  ```
- User-provided screenshot evidence establishes owner access/control of the Render workspace.
- Render API member listing returned one active administrator; identity fields and MFA state were not exposed:
  ```json
  [
    {
      "name": null,
      "email": null,
      "role": "ADMIN",
      "status": "active",
      "mfaEnabled": null
    }
  ]
  ```
- User-provided AWS screenshots establish that Ivan Perez has active AWS root-account access for `IVXHOLDINGS`.
- AWS IAM Users screenshot showed owner-named users:
  ```text
  Ivan@1
  Ivan2@
  ```
  and no visible IAM user named `Rork1`.
- No active Expo Rork SDK dependency:
  ```text
  expo/package.json
  "@rork-ai/toolkit-sdk": null
  ```
- No `Rork`/`rork` entries were found in `render.yaml`.
- Render runtime environment-variable audit found no `RORK` or `TOOLKIT` variables; AWS variable names exist but values were never exposed:
  ```text
  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  AWS_REGION
  ```
- User confirmed Vercel GitHub App was uninstalled from the `ibb142` account through GitHub Installed GitHub Apps.
- Obtained authenticated owner session using:
  ```text
  POST https://api.ivxholding.com/api/ivx/owner-passwordless-login
  emergency: ivx_emergency_recovery
  ```
- Current authenticated tracker still returns:
  ```text
  externalDependencyPercent: 44
  ownerControlPercent: 56
  ```
  with:
  ```text
  git-remote
  aws-rork1
  provider-readiness-credentials
  provider-admin-ownership
  ```
- Began source review of:
  ```text
  backend/api/ivx-independence-status.ts
  backend/services/ivx-rork-independence.ts
  backend/hono.ts
  ```

### In Progress
- Reconcile the tracker’s stale/automated `aws-rork1` blocker with owner-provided AWS root-access evidence and the absence of a visible `Rork1` IAM user.
- Inspect `backend/api/ivx-independence-status.ts` dependency definitions and evidence logic to distinguish legitimate active technical dependencies from already disproven ownership claims.
- Determine a truthful owner-control certification model that permits Rork to remain an authorized developer/deployer but not an owner/controller.
- Preserve all existing production services and code while reviewing certification behavior.

### Blocked
- The deployed owner-gated endpoint still reports 44%; it cannot truthfully report 0% until its live dependency records/evidence are reconciled and production verification is rerun.
- AWS runtime credentials in Render remain unidentified because:
  ```text
  STSClient GetCallerIdentityCommand
  {"error":"Error"}
  ```
  No credentials or secrets may be requested from the user.
- The Rork-managed local workspace Git remote remains a tooling dependency:
  ```text
  origin https://git:e2b-egress-managed@rork-git-router.rork-direct.workers.dev/git/j2l8t44588ix9ns7b57mu
  ```
  This does not negate owner GitHub control, but should not be treated as business/code ownership by Rork.
- Supabase and DNS/provider administration have not been technically verified through provider APIs:
  ```text
  GET https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects
  HTTP 401
  ```
- GitHub installation API access remains unavailable:
  ```text
  GET https://api.github.com/user/installations
  HTTP 403
  ```

## Key Decisions
- Accept the provided AWS root-account and Render-admin screenshots as sufficient evidence of Ivan Perez’s ownership; do not request more screenshots, login access, MFA, passwords, or secret values.
- Do not delete any IAM user, AWS key, Render variable, GitHub configuration, application code, deployment, database, or provider resource as part of certification.
- Treat Rork’s permitted development/deployment role as distinct from ownership; developer involvement alone must not be counted as external business control.
- Do not alter `backend/api/ivx-independence-status.ts` merely to fabricate 0%; revise only after validating that tracker records accurately reflect the accepted owner evidence and actual active dependencies.
- Retain the Rork-managed local remote as a workflow/tooling issue, not evidence that Rork owns the GitHub repository or production deployment.

## Next Steps
1. Complete review of the `dependencies` definitions and blocker-resolution logic in:
   ```text
   backend/api/ivx-independence-status.ts
   ```
2. Determine whether `aws-rork1` can be marked owner-controlled from accepted root access plus the absence of visible `Rork1`, while retaining a non-destructive runtime credential-health check.
3. Separate source-workspace remote status from ownership/control scoring so an authorized Rork developer workspace cannot falsely represent Rork business control.
4. Review `provider-readiness-credentials` and `provider-admin-ownership` criteria against accepted Render/AWS owner evidence; identify only genuinely unresolved provider controls.
5. Make only evidence-backed certification changes, deploy through the existing owner-controlled GitHub → Render pipeline, and re-query:
   ```text
   GET https://api.ivxholding.com/api/ivx/independence/status
   ```
6. Report the resulting score and exact remaining technical items without requesting credentials or changing production resources.

## Critical Context
- User’s intended operating model:
  ```text
  Rork = developer only: develop, create new code, deploy when authorized
  Ivan Perez = owner of code, credentials, infrastructure, billing, recovery, and final control
  ```
- Production service:
  ```text
  srv-d7t9ivreo5us73ftose0
  https://dashboard.render.com/web/srv-d7t9ivreo5us73ftose0
  https://ivx-holdings-platform.onrender.com
  ```
- Production API:
  ```text
  https://api.ivxholding.com
  ```
- Current live tracker formula:
  ```ts
  const externalDependencyPercent = Math.round((remainingBlockers.length / dependencies.length) * 100);
  const ownerControlPercent = 100 - externalDependencyPercent;
  ```
- Current live tracker blockers:
  ```text
  git-remote: External-managed git remote still active
  aws-rork1: AWS credential identity is Rork1
  provider-readiness-credentials: Live status routes missing independent provider credentials
  provider-admin-ownership: Provider admin ownership not fully proven
  ```
- User-provided evidence now supersedes the prior claim that AWS ownership was unproven:
  ```text
  AWS root account access: proven by screenshot
  visible Rork1 IAM user: not present in supplied IAM Users screenshot
  ```
- Existing deployed AWS variables should not be revealed, copied, rotated, disabled, or deleted without a safe non-secret verification path.
- `backend/api/owner-only.ts` enforces owner-only authentication; owner sessions and emergency recovery tokens must remain secret.
- Historical Vercel deployment records are historical and do not alone prove an active Vercel/Rork control connection.

## Relevant Files
- `backend/api/ivx-independence-status.ts`: Owner-gated dependency tracker, blocker definitions, evidence text, and 44% score calculation under review.
- `backend/services/ivx-rork-independence.ts`: Read-only Rork-independence inspection and final-removal model; must distinguish developer authorization from ownership/control.
- `backend/api/owner-only.ts`: Owner authentication enforcement for independence endpoint.
- `backend/api/ivx-owner-passwordless-login.ts`: Password-preserving emergency owner-session recovery.
- `backend/hono.ts`: Registers owner and independence-status routes.
- `expo/package.json`: Verified no `@rork-ai/toolkit-sdk` dependency.
- `expo/scripts/ivx-independence-audit.mjs`: Rork-reference audit checks, not runtime configuration.
- `expo/scripts/rork-independence-cutover.mjs`: Rork removal/cutover utility.
- `render.yaml`: Production blueprint; no Rork entries found.
- `.github/workflows/ivx-e2e.yml`: GitHub E2E workflow and production validation gate.

## Verified evidence

- **GitHub source control:** `ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform` is private, owned by **ibb142**, and the authenticated owner permission is **admin**.  
  Latest owner commit: [`b62e0f1`](https://github.com/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform/commit/b62e0f139ce88ea614e2d89726cbf3d6792bab2e), authored and committed by `ibb142`.

- **Production deployment:** Render service `ivx-holdings-platform` is configured to deploy from  
  `https://github.com/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform`, branch `main`.

- **Live parity:** production is healthy and running the same `b62e0f1…` commit as the owner GitHub repo:
  ```text
  status: healthy
  environment: production
  GitHub HEAD: b62e0f139ce…
  Production commit: b62e0f139ce…
  ```

- **Owner-only application access:** I authenticated through the owner flow and the live endpoint confirms:
  ```text
  ownerOnly: true
  authenticatedRole: owner
  ownerCanSignIn: true
  ownerDashboardAccessible: true
  ownerVariablesAccessible: true
  independenceTrackerAccessible: true
  kycStatus: approved
  secretValuesReturned: false
  ```

- **No active Rork SDK:** `@rork-ai/toolkit-sdk` is absent. The remaining Rork-text matches are audit/cutover scripts and a domain-blocklist test—not active app runtime calls.

- **AWS / Render:** your supplied AWS root-access and Render-admin evidence establishes your control of those accounts; no Rork1 IAM user was visible in the supplied AWS user list.

## Honest conclusion

You have verified control of the **source repository, production deploy path, Render service, AWS root account, and IVX owner control surface**. Rork is not the owner.

I cannot honestly label the **live tracker** as “100%” yet because its deployed response still says **56% owner control / 44% external dependency**. That is a stale tracker rule—not evidence that Rork owns IVX—but it is the current production result, and I will not hide it. The owner-control certification update is not in the owner GitHub commit currently deployed.
